A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are developing a new data base machine which is based on relational algebra, and which can execute join and projection for which a full file scan suffices, with a time proportional to the size of a file.

we are proposing a relational algebra machine GRACE which is a relational database machine with the following characteristics: 1) it is a relational algebra machine, i.e., it executes relational algebra expressions directly, 2) it is a filter machine, i.e. it executes the relational algebra operations by using filter processors, 3) it is a parallel machine, i.e, it has multiple processors which can work in parallel.

GRACE is a relational algebra machine which can execute all relational algebra operations including join, projection etc. at a speed comparable to that of the conventional machines for the light load operations and can execute the heavy load operations such as join, projection etc., at a speed comparable with that for the light load operation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the performance of the machine is improved to O(N+M) if the join operation is decomposed into two steps: 1) join of the two relations to produce a relation which is the union of all the possible join tuples and 2) elimination of the duplicate tuples from this union relation.
we can achieve the optimal performance of relational algebra operations on the machine which has a single processor by using the GRACE machine which has two processors.
